## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical patching of secret-driven TLS rotation, minimal no-downtime reload, and RBAC-friendly safeguards in CKAD scope. It emphasizes inter-container signaling, probe configuration, and availability during secret rotation.

## Key Concepts
- Secret mounting and readOnly
- InitContainer data preparation
- Sidecar for TLS rotation signaling
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Resource requests/limits
- PodDisruptionBudget
- In-cluster secret rotation verification and rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: fintech
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: cert-init
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh","-c","cp -r /tls/current/* /certs/ && echo ready > /shared/gateway.pid"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /certs
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "250m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      - name: tls-reloader
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh","-c","while true; do inotifywait -e modify,create,attrib /tls/current || true; if [ -f /shared/gateway.pid ]; then kill -USR1 $(cat /shared/gateway.pid); fi; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: gateway-tls
      - name: certs
      - name: shared
        emptyDir: {}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical CKAD skills: dynamic configuration via ConfigMaps, per-namespace isolation, InitContainers, health checks, logging, and network policy considerations.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps**: Enable dynamic feature flags without pod restarts
- **InitContainers**: Provide bootstrap tooling (curl) before the main container starts
- **Conditional sidecars**: Driven by ConfigMap values to enable canary deployments
- **Readiness and liveness probes**: Ensure controller and application health
- **PVC-backed logs**: Provide persistent storage for debugging and audit trails
- **NetworkPolicies**: Enforce zero-trust networking by restricting egress to known endpoints

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|----------------|
| **Polling Interval** | Frequent polls increase API load; infrequent polls delay flag propagation |
| **ConfigMap Updates** | Applications must watch or periodically read the ConfigMap to detect changes |
| **Sidecar Overhead** | Running a sidecar even when disabled consumes resources; consider whether the main container can react to flag changes directly |
| **Egress Restriction** | Locking down NetworkPolicy requires knowing all upstream dependencies upfront |
| **Log Persistence** | PVCs add operational complexity and cost; consider external logging solutions for production |

## Minimal YAML Skeleton

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
```

Tests understanding of InitContainer lifecycle, idempotent seeding patterns, and persistent cache management across pod restarts.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers and startup ordering
- ConfigMap-based seed script injection

```yaml
# Seed script ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: seed-scripts
data:
  seed.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -e
    if [ ! -f /cache/.seeded ]; then
      # Execute seeding logic here
      touch /cache/.seeded
    fi
---
# Deployment with InitContainer
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-cache
        image: busybox:1.35
        command: ['/bin/sh', '/scripts/seed.sh']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /scripts
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
      containers:
      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20

      - name: cache-volume
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a practical, namespace-scoped canary upgrade using standard CKAD tools: CronJob scheduling, patching Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets for config and credentials, and PVC-based logging. It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and JobTemplate execution
- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          containers:
          - name: upgrader
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "set -e; CANARY_TAG=$(kubectl get configmap canary-config -o jsonpath='{.data.tag}'); kubectl patch deployment my-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"my-app","image":"myrepo/my-app:${CANARY_TAG}"}]}}}}' --record; echo done; sleep 1"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement idempotent patches and roll back on failure?
- How to measure canary success (latency, error rate) before full rollout?
- How would this scale across many namespaces or deployments?
